gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states an independent fan-on versus fan-off phone temperature for any of the three picks; Android Authority measured the Belkin UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1 at 82°F with the fan on against 90°F with it off, while ESR's 6.5°F figure is only the maker's claim.
standout_why: I compared against six of the thirteen results. Macworld's ESR CryoBoost 25W review (cited) gives ESR's 6.5°F, 93.9°F and 25 dB figures as maker claims; its only own test is 0-50% in 'just over half an hour'. Macworld's ESR Foldable review, Macworld's Ugreen MagFlow Pro review, Pack Hacker and iThinkDiff likewise carry only maker temperature and dB figures. I could not check the rest: the cited Digital Camera World Anker Prime review returned only its title, the cited TechGearDen page failed on a certificate error, the Yahoo page returned 403, and I did not reach the 3-in-1 sections of the cited Macworld roundup. The Digital Camera World title ('unbelievable cooling') suggests it may hold temperature readings for the Anker, so the score is 2, not 3.
decides: It does not overturn ESR as the value pick, but it changes the grounds. ChatGPT's 'strong independent test results for speed and cooling' is half supported for the ESR: Macworld tested speed, and no page I opened measured its cooling. The Belkin is the only pick with a named fan-on/fan-off measurement (8°F cooler surface, 6 to 8°F cooler battery, on a Galaxy S25 Edge, short of Belkin's 12°F claim). The Anker has one named absolute reading (about 33°C after 30 minutes, Makurin). A shopper who wants measured cooling evidence has it for the Belkin at $129.99 (Android Authority's listed price) and partly for the Anker; for the ESR at $109.99 the evidence is the maker's own 6.5°F or 7.2°F claim.

findings.label: Phone glass surface peak, fan on vs fan off (Android Authority, Brady Snyder)
findings.value: 82°F fan on vs 90°F fan off (27.8°C vs 32.2°C), 8°F difference
findings.source_title: Android Authority: Qi2 active cooling wireless charger test (Belkin UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1)
findings.note: Article dated 2026-02-14. Phone was a Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge, not an iPhone. It was drained to zero and charged for 30 minutes, once with the fan on and once off. Surface was read with a Pixel 9 Pro XL's temperature sensor. Room temperature is not reported. The °C values are my conversions.

findings.label: Phone battery temperature across five 10-minute charging intervals (Android Authority, Brady Snyder)
findings.value: 91.3°F after interval 1 (fan on); 98.1°F, 98.8°F and 100.8°F after intervals 2-4 (fan off); back to 94.8°F after interval 5 (fan on); 6 to 8°F cooler on average with the fan
findings.source_title: Android Authority: Qi2 active cooling wireless charger test (Belkin UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1)
findings.note: Battery sensor read with the Physics Toolbox app on a Galaxy S25 Edge. 6 to 8°F is 3.3 to 4.4°C (my conversion). Belkin claims up to 12°F; the author says he never saw the full 12°F. The article lists the charger at $129.99 on Amazon.
